name: Rape and sexual assault
summary: Any sexual act without free consent. You can report at any police station, get free medical treatment at any hospital, and your identity must be kept confidential.
evidence: Seek medical care as soon as you can; any hospital must treat you free
If possible, keep the clothes you wore in a paper bag (not plastic)
Write down what you remember: date, time, place, the person, anyone you told
Messages, calls or photos related to the incident
Names of anyone who saw you before or after
documents: Any ID proof (Aadhaar, voter ID, college ID)
Medical / MLC report from the hospital
Copy of the FIR (you are entitled to a free copy)

name: Sexual harassment and molestation
summary: Unwelcome touching, groping, sexual remarks, gestures or showing sexual content. In public places, on transport or anywhere else.
evidence: Date, time, exact place and route (bus number, train, shop)
Description of the person
Names or numbers of witnesses
CCTV locations nearby (ask police to secure footage quickly)
Photos or video if safely taken
documents: Ticket or travel proof if on transport

name: Stalking
summary: Someone repeatedly follows you, contacts you after you said no, or monitors your phone, email or social media.
evidence: A dated log of every incident
Screenshots of calls and messages showing number/profile and time
Proof you told them to stop
Photos of the person or vehicle if safe
Witnesses
documents: Call records (you can request from your telecom provider)

name: Online harassment and cyberstalking
summary: Abusive messages, threats, fake profiles, hacking or monitoring your accounts online.
evidence: Screenshots showing the profile URL, username, message and date-time
Profile links (copy the URL)
Do not delete chats; export them if possible
Report the profile on the platform and screenshot the report
Keep the device; electronic evidence needs a BSA Section 63 certificate
documents: BSA Section 63 certificate for electronic evidence (police can guide)

name: Blackmail, sextortion and leaked or morphed images
summary: Someone threatens to share private or morphed images unless you pay or do something, or has already shared them.
evidence: Do NOT pay; it usually leads to more demands
Screenshot the threats with the profile/number and date-time
Save links where images were posted
Do not delete the conversation
Report the content to the platform for takedown and to StopNCII.org
documents: Payment proof if you already paid

name: Hidden cameras and voyeurism
summary: Being secretly watched, photographed or filmed in a private situation, or such images being shared.
evidence: Note the location and time
Do not touch a hidden device; photograph it and inform police
Links if images were shared

name: Domestic violence
summary: Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional or economic abuse by a husband, partner or family member you live or lived with.
evidence: Photos of injuries and damaged property
Medical records of any treatment
A dated diary of incidents
Messages, voice notes or call recordings of threats
Names of neighbours or relatives who know
documents: Marriage certificate or proof of relationship
Proof of shared household (ration card, rent agreement, bills)
Bank statements if money is withheld

name: Dowry harassment
summary: Demands for money, gold or property from you or your family in connection with marriage, and harassment for not meeting them.
evidence: List of gifts, gold and money given, with dates
Wedding photos showing gifts
Messages or recordings of demands
Bank transfers
documents: Bills or receipts for jewellery and gifts (stridhan list)

name: Sexual harassment at work or college
summary: Sexual harassment by a boss, colleague, client, teacher or anyone at your workplace or institution.
evidence: Emails, chats and messages
Dates and places of each incident
Names of colleagues who witnessed or you confided in
Any earlier complaints you made
documents: Appointment letter or proof of employment / enrolment
Copy of your organisation's POSH policy if available

name: Acid attack
summary: Throwing or attempting to throw acid. Every hospital must give free immediate treatment.
evidence: Get to a hospital immediately; pour plenty of clean water on the area
Names of witnesses
Any earlier threats from the person

name: Sexual abuse of a girl under 18
summary: Any sexual act, touch or harassment involving someone under 18 is an offence under POCSO, regardless of consent.
evidence: Take the child to a doctor; treatment is free
Write down what the child said, in her words, without pressing for details
Do not confront the accused yourself
documents: Child's age proof (birth certificate / school record)

name: Threats and intimidation
summary: Threats to hurt you, your family, your reputation or property.
evidence: Screenshots or recordings of the threats
Dates and witnesses
